newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF CELTIC PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF CELTIC PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of Celtic players ahead of Sunday's Scottish premier division match against Rangers:

Stewart Kerr (goalkeeper, age 22). A product of Celtic Boys Club who has made a huge impression since replacing former No.1 Gordon Marshall after Marshall was sent off eight minutes from time against Motherwell in October. Has kept his place ever since and now been called up to the Scottish senior squad.
Tommy Boyd (defender, 31). Scottish international defender who has also played for Motherwell and Chelsea. Has great pace and uses that to overlap down the wing whenever possible.

Tosh McKinlay (defender, 32). Another Scottish international defender now in his third season with Celtic after many years at both Dundee and Hearts, but he ironically played for Celtic Boys Club as a youngster. Has the unusual middle name of Valley. Tosh is his nickname, correct first name is Tom.

Jackie McNamara (defender, 21). Broke into the Celtic side last season and played so well was voted Scotland's Young Player of the Year at the end of the campaign. Has recently won his first international cap and looks set for a great future.

Erico Annoni (defender, 30). Shaven-headed hard-tackling Italian defender who joined Celtic for 500,000 pounds from Roma last month. Turned down offers to stay in Italy, or go to France or England, due to the persuasive powers of Celtic's Italian striker Paolo di Canio.

Malky Mackay (defender, 25). Worked as a bank clerk while playing amateur football for Queens Park. Injuries have hampered his progress at Celtic but there was no hiding his joy when his headed goal put Celtic 1-0 ahead and on their way to victory against Rangers in the Scottish Cup last week.

Alan Stubbs (defender, 25), Marked his debut for Celtic after his expensive summer signing from Bolton by getting sent off against Aberdeen after 74 minutes. Besides that has settled down well to his new surroundings.

Peter Grant (midfielder, 31). Tenacious midfielder who made his Celtic debut as an 18-year-old in 1984 and is now approaching 400 games for his only club. Has represented Scotland at every level -- Schools, Youth, Under-21, "B" and has two full caps from playing against England and Chile in 1989.
Paul McStay (midfielder, 32). Scotland's third most capped player with 74 caps. Like Grant, Celtic is his only club and has played over 500 matches for them since making his debut in January 1982.

Paolo di Canio (striker, 28), Distinctive-looking Italian striker who usually wears white boots. Scored with a coolly-taken penalty against Rangers in Celtic's 2-0 Scottish Cup win last week. Has scored 13 times in what has been a fine debut season in Scotland, but he was fined 10,000 pounds by the club for being sent off against Hearts in November.
Andreas Thom (striker, 31), German striker now in his second season at Celtic, although he is more on the fringes of the team than he was last year. Has scored eight goals so far this campaign.
